title: Origin Bancorp, Inc. Reports Earnings for Third | Origin Bank
summary: Origin Bancorp, Inc. Origin Bancorp, Inc. (TXSE: OBK) (“Origin,” “we,” “our” or the “Company”), the holding company for Origin Bank (the “Bank”), today announced net income of $37.8 million, or $1.22 diluted earnings per share (“EPS”), for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $33.8 million, or $1.09 diluted EPS, for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Pre-tax, pre-provision (“PTPP”)(1) earnings were $50.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $43.2 million for the linked quarter.


“Our third quarter results reflect the discipline and commitment of our team and the progress we are making through Optimize Origin,” said Drake Mills, chairman, president and CEO of Origin Bancorp, Inc. “We are delivering higher levels of profitability while deepening relationships and investing intentionally in our franchise. I am proud of what we accomplished this quarter, and we know there is more work ahead as we continue delivering long-term value to our shareholders.”


(1) PTPP earnings is a non-GAAP financial measure, please see the last few pages of this document for a reconciliation of this alternative financial measure to its most directly comparable GAAP measure.


***Optimize Origin***


• In January 2025, we announced our Optimize Origin initiative to drive elite financial performance and enhance our award-winning culture, and it continues to be an important part of our corporate DNA.


• Built on three primary pillars:


◦ Productivity, Delivery & Efficiency


◦ Balance Sheet Optimization


◦ Culture & Employee Engagement


• As announced in our Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Earnings Release, our near term ROAA run rate target is 1.15% or higher by 4Q26, as we continue towards our ultimate top quartile ROAA target.


**Financial Highlights**


• The Company continued to deliver strong performance, and in some cases, record performance across numerous key financial metrics including, but not limited to, net income, net interest income, fully tax-equivalent net interest margin (“NIM-FTE”) and diluted earnings per share.


• Net income was $37.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, reflecting an increase of $3.9 million, or 11.6%, compared to the linked quarter.


• Non-interest income was $18.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, reflecting an increase of $2.7 million, or 17.5%, compared to the linked quarter.


• Our NIM-FTE increased two basis points to 3.94% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended June 30, 2026.


• Annualized ROAA was 1.47% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, reflecting an increase of 12 basis points, compared to the quarter ended June 30, 2026.


• Total loans held for investment (“LHFI”) were $8.09 billion at September 30, 2026, reflecting an increase of $20.6 million, or 0.3%, compared to June 30, 2026. LHFI, excluding mortgage warehouse lines of credit, were $7.65 billion at September 30, 2026, reflecting an increase of $170.6 million, or 2.3%, compared to June 30, 2026.


• During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, we repurchased 272,927 shares of our common stock at an average price of $54.21 per share, including commissions and applicable excise taxes. At September 30, 2026, $106.8 million remains available for share repurchases under the share repurchase program.


• In October 2026, our board approved an increase in our quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.28 per share, a 12% increase. Combined with the $0.10 per share increase approved in April 2026, the quarterly dividend has increased from $0.15 to $0.28 per share, or 87%, reflecting our strong balance sheet and durable earnings.


**Results of Operations for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026**


**Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin**


Net interest income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $95.1 million, an increase of $2.9 million, or 3.2%, compared to the quarter ended June 30, 2026. The expansion in net interest income was primarily driven by a $4.3 million increase in interest income, which was partially offset by a $1.4 million increase in interest expense.


The $4.3 million increase in interest income was primarily due to an increase of $3.6 million in interest income on loans held for investment, mainly driven by higher average loan balances, which contributed $1.6 million of the increase. An additional $1.4 million of the increase resulted from one additional calendar day during the current quarter, while the remaining $648,000 was attributable to higher loan yields.


The $1.4 million increase in interest expense was primarily attributable to a $2.1 million increase in interest expense on interest-bearing deposits, partially offset by a $740,000 decrease in interest expense on FHLB advances and other borrowings. The increase in interest expense on interest-bearing deposits was primarily attributable to higher average balances, which increased interest expense by $1.1 million. This impact was primarily related to higher average money market deposit balances, which increased interest expense by $1.6 million, partially offset by lower average balances in interest-bearing demand deposits. Higher rates and one extra day in the quarter contributed another $1.0 million to the increase in interest expense on deposits. The decrease in interest expense on FHLB and other borrowings was mainly attributable to lower average borrowing balances, which decreased interest expense by approximately $762,000.


The Federal Reserve Board sets various benchmark rates, including the federal funds rate, and thereby influences the general market rates of interest, including loan and deposit rates offered by financial institutions. On October 29, 2025, and December 10, 2025, the Federal Reserve Board reduced the federal funds target rate range by 25 basis points each, to a range of 3.50% to 3.75%. On September 16, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board raised the federal funds target rate range by 25 basis points, to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%.


Our NIM-FTE was 3.94% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up two basis points from the linked quarter and 29 basis points from the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The yield earned on interest-earning assets was 5.76%, representing a two-basis-point increase and a 13-basis-point decrease compared to the linked quarter and the quarter ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The average rate paid on total interest-bearing liabilities was 2.70%, representing a three-basis-point increase from the linked quarter and down 52 basis points compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025.


**Credit Quality**


The table below includes key credit quality information:


Our results included a total provision for credit losses of $2.6 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $65,000 for the linked quarter, which includes the provision for loan credit losses, the off-balance sheet commitment credit losses and any provision for security credit losses. The increase was primarily the result of new loan production and an increase in net loan charge-offs, offset by credit migration improvement during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, resulting in provision expense for loan credit losses of $2.9 million compared to a net benefit provision of $373,000 during the linked quarter. For the current quarter, we recorded reserves of $6.1 million related to new loan production and $1.3 million related to net charge-offs not previously reserved, which was primarily offset by $5.2 million in reserve releases related to net credit migration. Net credit migration reflects the combined impact of loan risk rating changes, specific reserve adjustments, and loan balance movements, such as loan balance changes and payoffs.


The ALCL totaled $98.4 million at September 30, 2026, a $190,000 increase compared to the ALCL as of June 30, 2026, and was 1.22% as a percentage of LHFI at both September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026.


Past due 30 to 89 days and still accruing increased $5.1 million to $10.3 million at September 30, 2026, when compared to June 30, 2026, and represented 0.13% of total LHFI, compared to 0.06% as of June 30, 2026. The increase in loans past due 30 to 89 days and still accruing was primarily driven by increases of $2.5 million, $1.7 million and $1.1 million in the commercial and industrial, commercial real estate and construction/land/land development sectors, respectively. 100% of the increases were in the 30 to 59 days past due category.


Total nonperforming LHFI decreased $6.1 million at September 30, 2026, when compared to June 30, 2026. The decrease in nonperforming LHFI was driven by decreases in the sectors of commercial real estate, construction/land/land development and commercial and industrial, offset by an increase in single-family residential real estate nonperforming LHFI. $1.6 million of the decline in nonperforming LHFI was a result of net paydowns or payoffs of nonperforming loans, primarily in the construction/land/land development sector, impacted by the questioned banker activity first disclosed during the quarter ended June 30, 2024. During the current quarter, six loan relationships totaling $2.2 million previously classified as nonperforming LHFI were transferred to other real estate owned (“OREO”).


Net charge-offs were $2.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, reflecting an increase of $2.2 million compared to the quarter ended June 30, 2026, primarily reflecting lower recoveries of $1.5 million and an increase of $728,000 in charge-offs. The decrease in recoveries was primarily the result of lower recoveries in the commercial and industrial loan sector and the increase in charge-offs was primarily a result of higher charge-offs in the commercial real estate and commercial and industrial loan sectors.


**Noninterest Income**


Noninterest income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $18.1 million, an increase of $2.7 million, or 17.5%, from the linked quarter, primarily driven by an increase of $1.7 million in equity method investment income and an increase of $452,000 in insurance commission and fee income.


The $1.7 million increase in equity method investment income was primarily driven by an increase in Argent investment income of $1.2 million compared to the linked quarter and a reduction of $499,000 in limited partnership equity investment loss during the current quarter compared to the linked quarter.


The components of equity method investment income (loss) are as follows:


The $452,000 increase in insurance commission and fee income is primarily the result of an increase in life and health direct bill commission income.


**Noninterest Expense**


Noninterest expense for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $62.5 million, a decrease of $1.9 million, or 3.0% from the linked quarter. The decrease was primarily due to a decrease of $869,000 in other expenses along with a decrease of $543,000 in professional services.


The $869,000 decrease in other expense was primarily due to a $2.2 million release of contingency reserve offset by an $883,000 charge, both of which relate to the settlement of certain litigation involving the questioned banker activity first disclosed during the quarter ended June 30, 2024.


The $543,000 decrease in professional services was primarily due to a $452,000 decrease in consultant fees related to contract renegotiations that occurred during the first half of the 2026 fiscal year.


**Financial Condition**


The table below discloses the changes in certain balance sheet metrics:


*Loans*


- Excluding mortgage warehouse lines of credit, LHFI increased $170.6 million, or 2.3%, from June 30, 2026. The increase was primarily driven by increases of $78.1 million, $66.8 million, and $24.0 million in construction/land/land development, owner-occupied commercial real estate loans and non-owner-occupied commercial real estate, respectively. These increases were partially offset by a decrease of $19.1 million in commercial and industrial loans.
- Mortgage warehouse lines of credit at September 30, 2026, were $439.7 million, a decrease of $150.0 million, or 25.4%, from $589.7 million at June 30, 2026, and a decrease of $33.3 million, or 7.0%, compared to September 30, 2025.


*Securities*


• Accumulated other comprehensive loss, net of taxes, primarily associated with unrealized losses within the available for sale portfolio, was $96.4 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $35.6 million, or 58.5%, from the linked quarter and an increase of $35.2 million, or 57.6% from September 30, 2025.


• The weighted average effective duration for the total securities portfolio was 4.65 years as of September 30, 2026, compared to 4.08 years as of June 30, 2026.


*Deposits*


• The increase in average deposits for the current quarter compared to linked quarter was primarily due to increases of $217.0 million and $80.0 million in money market and noninterest-bearing deposits, respectively. Offsetting these increases was a decrease of $79.9 million in average interest-bearing demand deposits.


• At September 30, 2026, June 30, 2026, and September 30, 2025, average noninterest-bearing deposits as a percentage of average total deposits were 24.9%, 24.6% and 23.1%, respectively.


*Borrowings*


• The decrease in the current quarter borrowings compared to the linked quarter primarily reflects lower FHLB short- term borrowings as the linked quarter included $125.0 million of additional borrowings used primarily to meet seasonal liquidity needs.


*Subordinate debentures*


• Total subordinated debentures at September 30, 2026, compared to September 30, 2025, declined primarily due to the redemption of $74.0 million in subordinated debentures during the quarter ended December 31, 2025, in conjunction with our Optimize Origin initiative.


*Capital*


• The decrease in shareholder’s equity at September 30, 2026, compared to the linked quarter was mainly due to $35.6 million of other comprehensive loss, net of tax, as well as $14.8 million in common share repurchases and $7.9 million of dividends declared, partially offset by net income of $37.8 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


• Uses of regulatory capital since the beginning of 2025 consist of the following:


◦ Repurchased 1,106,466 shares of our common stock at an average price of $42.97 per share, for a total of $47.5 million, including commissions and applicable excise taxes. There is currently $106.8 million remaining available for share repurchases under the share repurchase program.


◦ Redeemed $143.6 million of subordinated debentures, including the amortization of the original issue discount and fair value mark.


◦ Declared $39.4 million in dividends to our shareholders, excluding dividends declared in October 2026.

**About Origin**


Origin Bancorp, Inc. is a financial holding company headquartered in Ruston, Louisiana. Origin’s wholly owned bank subsidiary, Origin Bank, was founded in 1912 in Choudrant, Louisiana. Deeply rooted in Origin’s history is a culture committed to providing personalized relationship banking to businesses, municipalities, and personal clients to enrich the lives of the people in the communities it serves. Origin provides a broad range of financial services and currently operates more than 57 locations in Dallas/Fort Worth, East Texas, Houston, North Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and the Florida Panhandle. In addition, Origin provides a broad range of insurance agency products and services through its wholly owned insurance agency subsidiary, Forth Insurance, LLC. For more information, visit www.origin.bank and[www.forthinsurance.com.](http://www.forthinsurance.com./)


**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


Origin reports its results in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America ("GAAP"). However, management believes that certain supplemental non-GAAP financial measures may provide meaningful information to investors that is useful in understanding Origin's results of operations and underlying trends in its business. These non-GAAP financial measures are supplemental and should be viewed in addition to, and not as an alternative for, Origin's reported results prepared in accordance with GAAP. The following are the non-GAAP measures used in this release: PTPP earnings, PTPP ROAA, tangible book value per common share, and ROATCE.


Please see the last few pages of this release for reconciliations of non-GAAP measures to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP.
